final_candidates.decision_summary: K498 is a key m102.4 contact residue at the NiV-G/antibody interface; alanine removes the critical charged side chain likely involved in antibody recognition while minimizing structural disruption.
Y501 is positioned at the core of the m102.4 epitope; alanine removes the aromatic ring contributing to hydrophobic and hydrogen-bonding contacts with the antibody paratope.
L499 sits adjacent to K498 and Y501 in the m102.4 binding interface; alanine removes a hydrophobic contact contributing to antibody binding energy while being less likely to disrupt receptor binding.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve the top-3 ranking; the current candidates represent the most promising escape mutations based on structural reasoning.
